title: Silent cutover tactical cheat notes
content:
Context / intent:
This is a private scratchpad for a low-noise, low-attention cutover approach ("silent cutover") where we transition cohorts to a new model variant with minimal visible churn and no scheduled maintenance window. The goal is to let product traffic progressively converge on the new variant while preserving latency SLOs and minimizing false-positive rollbacks caused by client-side retries or load spikes.

High-level idea:
- Warm shadowing + micro-cohorts + affinity pinning.
- Start with entirely shadowed traffic (no client-visible responses) to build per-client stability signals.
- Flip a tiny anchored cohort (0.05% of active clients) to real responses using sticky pin; observe metrics and compare to shadow baseline.
- Expand cohorts in geometric progression (0.05 -> 0.2 -> 0.8 -> 3 -> 10%) with guardrails.
- Use metadata routing (client-seg header, region, auth level) so we can detach at cohort boundaries.

Preflight checklist (quick):
- [ ] Canary build flagged and immutably tagged in registry (image + model hash).
- [ ] Backfill KV cache warmers for likely hot prefixes (run during shadowing).
- [ ] Canary runtime config: batch_size cap, kv_cache TTL, quantization profile pinned.
- [ ] Instrumentation hooks live: token-latency histogram, backend queue length, kv-miss rate, mem/gpu pressure, sampler trace id.
- [ ] Alerts added to temporary channel: latency > 2x baseline (1m), error rate delta > 0.5% absolute (5m), tail-p95 > baseline+75ms (1m).
- [ ] Rollforward plan drafted (fast expand on green): seq and thresholds.
- [ ] Rollback playbook ready: pinned older variant + fast pinback API call + drain policy.

Telemetry signals (what I will watch):
- Client-visible error rate (4xx vs 5xx) by cohort
- Token-level latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) and spike windows
- Request amplification (client retries / repeat requests)
- Cost delta per 1k requests (batching efficiency change)
- Key metric regressions: hallucination signal (if available), BLEU/ROUGE on eval hooks, rerank score drift
- Upstream dependency latencies (model serving queue, feature store)
- Cohort stickiness: % of clients that stay after first successful response

Safety thresholds (proposal, adjustable):
- Immediate rollback if 5xx > baseline + 0.5% for 3 consecutive 1m windows across >2 regions
- Pause expansion if p95 increases by >100ms sustained for 5m
- Pause if KV miss rate increases by >2x baseline for 5m
- If client amplification (retries) increases by >20% in 10m, revert cohort and investigate

Cohort expansion plan (sticky pin semantics):
- Phase 0: Shadow only for 48h across 5% of traffic (no client-facing output). Collect logs + offline comparators.
- Phase 1: Anchor cohort 0.05% active clients (sticky pin via account id) for 30m observation window.
- Phase 2: Move to 0.2% for 60m if all thresholds green.
- Phase 3: 0.8% for 90m, begin small region expansion.
- Phase 4: 3% for 2h; open to non-critical user segments.
- Phase 5: 10% for 4h; monitor cost and quality metrics.
- Phase 6: 100% ramp only if green across last 6h and no open incidents.

Notes on pin implementation:
- Use client-id + session-hash to create stable pins (so experiment is deterministic per client).
- Fallback keys: if client id missing, use IP first-byte bucket + device-fingerprint to avoid blackholes.
- Maintain mapping in ephemeral store with TTL 30d; allow manual override via admin API.

Edge cases and mitigations:
- Bot-heavy clients: they can skew early signals. Filter by UA / rate pattern and exclude from anchor cohorts.
- Third-party proxies (shared IPs): prefer account-id pinning over IP to avoid mass flip.
- Cold-start cost: for short bursts we may see batching efficiency drop; monitor per-minute token cost.
- Client SDKs that aggressively retry: add quickserver-side dedupe of identical request-id for 10s window.

Hypotheses to validate in Phase 0 (shadowing):
- H1: New variant's p95 latency is within +50ms of current baseline for 95% of request types.
- H2: Batch size distribution will not drop below X (where X = current 25th percentile) causing >10% cost increase.
- H3: Early regression signals correlate with specific prompt families (identify via prompt-tagging).

Quick runbook (what I do in first 30m after Phase 1 flip):
- Confirm canary tag and runtime config active (ops dashboard)
- Verify shadow vs real histograms lined up (side-by-side)
- Sanity check sample responses for a handful of high-volume clients (manual QA)
- Watch alerts channel for immediate noise; be ready to call rollback at first sign of sustained error elevation
- If everything green, expand to next cohort size and note timestamps for each expansion

Manual rollback steps (fast path):
1) Call admin pinback API: /admin/pinback?cohort=anchorX -> immediate rebind to previous model
2) Increase routing weight to standby pool for 5m to drain new variant instances
3) Trigger cache warming for previous variant (warmers) to reduce latency blip
4) Postmortem stub: start draft with timeline, metrics, suspected root cause (tickets: RWINF-5126)

Open questions / todo (me):
- Decide exact geometric multiplier for cohort expansion (2.5x vs 4x). Preference: 4x for faster confidence, but meh risk.
- Add a temporary dedupe request-id header to client SDKs before flip? Need eng SDK lead signoff.
- Who is the on-call responder for model-quality regressions (not infra)? Loop in Maya from applied-ml.
- Should we bake an auto-pause hook in rollout controller vs manual pause? MVP = manual.

Snippets / command cheats (ops):
- list active pins: curl -H "Auth: bearer $TOKEN" https://internal.redwood/api/pins?cohort=anchorX
- force pinback: curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/admin/pinback -d '{"cohort":"anchorX","target":"prev-stable"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json"
- sample traffic shadow collector: k run one-off-shadow --image=... --env=SHADOW=1 --tail 2000

Notes to self (writing reasons):
- This doc lives in users/ because it's my quick tactical plan; will convert to shared_drives/engineering if we want to standardize after first run.
- Keep expansion conservative until we have region-level p99 approximations wired up.

Last run comments (draft):
- If we try this with RWINF-5126 canary: ensure model hash has deterministic seed for top-k sampling; nondeterminism caused one client cluster to see more variance last time.
- Samir to follow up on SDK retry header by 2026-03-07. Lena to validate warmers script.

End of scratchpad.
